items.title: EOCO to trace and recover assets linked to Asante Berko bribery probe
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) says it will trace and, where supported by evidence, pursue the recovery of assets and proceeds linked to suspected criminal conduct in the Ghanaian aspect of the Asante Kwaku Berko bribery case. The move follows Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States and the escalation of investigations into persons and transactions in Ghana potentially connected to the case. In a statement issued on Monday, August 10, EOCO said asset tracing and recovery would form a key part of its investigation. “Importantly, and consistent with its statutory mandate, asset tracing and recovery form an integral part of EOCO’s investigative plan in this matter,” the Office said. According to EOCO, investigators will seek to establish whether any proceeds, benefits, assets or property were derived from or connected to suspected criminal conduct. Where such assets are identified, and the law permits, the Office said it would take appropriate steps towards their preservation and recovery. “Where the law permits,” EOCO said, it will pursue “the appropriate measures for their preservation, recovery and restitution to the State.” EOCO explained that its mandate goes beyond establishing whether criminal offences have been committed and extends to recovering resources unlawfully acquired or dissipated through economic and organised crime. “EOCO’s mandate extends beyond establishing whether an offence has been committed,” the statement said. “Where economic or organised crime results in the unlawful acquisition or dissipation of public resources, the recovery of such resources is an essential component of the investigative and enforcement process.” The Office said investigators would consequently follow the financial trail as the probe progresses, examining relevant transactions and potential beneficiaries. “The Office therefore intends to follow the evidence and financial trail, including any relevant transactions, beneficiaries, assets and proceeds that may fall within its jurisdiction,” it said. Ghanaian investigation EOCO said the investigation stems from a request it received last year from its United States counterparts in connection with an alleged bribery scheme involving Mr Berko during his time in the private sector. The request sought information on specific individuals in Ghana considered relevant to the US investigation, including a former Minister of State and some public servants. EOCO subsequently began preliminary work in collaboration with the Office of the Attorney-General and Ministry of Justice while monitoring proceedings in the United States. Following Mr Berko’s conviction, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice engaged the appropriate US authorities to obtain evidence, records and other information required to advance investigations in Ghana. The Attorney-General has since directed EOCO to escalate its investigations as the relevant information is obtained through lawful channels. EOCO, however, stressed that any asset recovery or other enforcement action would be evidence-based and undertaken in accordance with Ghanaian law. It also cautioned that Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States does not automatically establish criminal liability against any individual in Ghana.

items.title: At least 20 dead as major quake rocks Colombia, other countries
items.description: A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and neighbouring Latin American countries on Monday, with medical teams rushing to help victims after buildings were damaged or collapsed in several cities. The death toll after the earthquake has risen to at least 20, authorities said. The Colombian geological service and its American counterpart USGS put the magnitude at 7.4, with an epicentre 100km underground in the west of the country. Colombia had initially put it at 6.6. In the town of Pereira, 18 people were killed and others were trapped in buildings that collapsed, Mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio . “The situation is critical,” Salazar said after the quake centered in neighbouring Choco province. In Manizales, two people were killed, Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas said in an interview with Blu Radio . Colombian officials said they did not fear a tsunami after the early-morning quake, which was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela. It prompted building evacuations in Bogota, AFP reporters saw, while news footage showed collapsed buildings elsewhere in the country. The governor of Colombia’s Choco province wrote on X that there were injuries and serious damage to buildings in the department’s capital Quibdo. News outlets aired footage of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Pereira and Manizales in a tourist region called Eje Cafetero. ‘Strong, really strong’ “There is no electricity or cell phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house,” Martha Estrada, a 66-year-old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP . Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia’s third largest city, also reported “major damage” that was being evaluated with drones. At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city, with people trapped inside, the mayor said. The city has requested teams from Bogota and Medellin to aid in rescue efforts, he added. “The quake was very, very strong,” said Valeria Polo, a 29 year old content creator in Bogota. Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said. These airports serve Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, the agency wrote on X. Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings. President Abelardo de la Espriella announced he would travel to the quake-hit region. News outlets aired footage of some buildings with their facades ripped off by the quake. In Bogota some people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw. Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage.

items.title: $1 million bribe: Former Power Minister Kwabena Donkor denies allegations, threatens legal action
items.description: Former Power Minister Dr Kwabena Donkor has strongly denied any involvement in the bribery allegations surrounding former Goldman Sachs banker Asante Kwaku Berko, insisting that he has never met Mr Berko, demanded money from him or received any personal benefit connected with the power deal. Dr Donkor’s lawyers, Cavendish Chambers, said their client had “absolutely no knowledge” of the allegations linking him to the US bribery case and had “completely and emphatically” denied any knowledge of a request or demand for money. The lawyers issued a statement on Monday, August 10, as speculation about the identity of a former Ghanaian Minister of Power named in the US case continued to circulate on social media. A US federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, convicted Mr Berko on August 6, 2026, in a case involving allegations that he participated in a scheme to bribe Ghanaian government officials to secure a power plant project for Turkish energy company Aksa Enerji Uretim A.S. US prosecutors said Mr Berko was involved in efforts to secure and manage the deal between Aksa and the Government of Ghana while he was an executive director in Goldman Sachs’ investment banking division. ‘I have never met Berko’ In the statement signed by Head of Chambers of the law firm, K.T. Hammond, Dr Donkor acknowledged that he was the Minister of Power during the period in question, describing that fact as a matter of public record. He also confirmed that the Ministry of Power negotiated with Aksa Energy for the generation of electricity in Ghana at the height of the country’s power crisis, popularly known as dumsor . According to the lawyers, however, Dr Donkor said the negotiations did not involve any personal arrangement between himself and Mr Berko. In emphatic terms, the lawyers said their client maintained that: “He has never met the said Mr Asante Berko all his life;” “He never discussed any personal benefit of any value whatsoever with Mr Asante Berko or any other person for that matter;” “He never authorised any person to discuss any such matters on his behalf;” “He never received any money in any denomination or any personal benefit of any value from Mr Asante Berko or any other person;” and any person who may have made a criminal demand in his name did so for that person’s own benefit. The lawyers said Dr Donkor further maintained that he had not seen any evidence from the US proceedings linking him personally to a demand for or receipt of money. Turkey trip explained The former minister also addressed the reported visit to Turkey by Ghanaian officials during the negotiations. His lawyers said a technical team comprising representatives of the country’s electricity-sector stakeholders travelled to Istanbul to inspect the equipment intended for the proposed power generation project. They described the exercise as a “regular practice of pre-shipment inspection” and stressed that Dr Donkor was not part of any alleged effort to solicit personal benefits from the project. According to the statement, Dr Donkor said: “According to our client at no point in the course of this negotiation did he once set eyes on the said Mr Asante Berko nor has he since.” ‘Senior Ghana Official’ reference The lawyers also challenged any attempt to equate references in the US case to a request for money for a “Senior Ghana Official” with evidence that Dr Donkor himself had demanded or received a bribe. “Our client does not understand that any evidence was led in the US trial which linked him with demanding or receiving any money, cedis or dollars or anything of value to him personally,” the statement said. “He does not accept that evidence that some other person or persons claimed that they required money from their principals for the benefit of “Senior Ghana Official” or any other title holder metamorphosed into any evidence of criminality or wrong doing against him.” The US Justice Department’s public account of the case has previously said that Berko and co-conspirators discussed paying $1 million to the Ghanaian Minister of Power responsible for securing key approvals for the project. It also separately alleged payments to other Ghanaian officials. Legal action threat Cavendish Chambers said its client had instructed the firm to make his position clear to the public and warned that publications or statements that sought to impugn his reputation and integrity would attract legal action. The lawyers said such conduct “SHALL result in immediate legal proceedings.” The statement adds a significant new dimension to calls for investigations into the Ghanaian side of the Berko case following his conviction in the United States. The OSP has disclosed that it provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the FBI in the prosecution, while Ghanaian authorities have indicated that the local aspects of the case require further examination. The US case itself concerned allegations of bribery involving Ghanaian officials in connection with the Aksa power project. Mr Berko faces a maximum sentence of 30 years following his conviction.

items.title: Burkina : l’ANPFI évalue l’impact de la crise sécuritaire sur les institutions de microfinance partenaires
items.description: Burkina : l’ANPFI évalue l’impact de la crise sécuritaire sur les institutions de microfinance partenaires Ouagadougou, 10 août 2026 (AIB)- L’Agence nationale de promotion de la finance inclusive (ANPFI) a organisé, lundi à Ouagadougou, une rencontre consacrée à l’examen et à la validation du rapport provisoire de l’étude sur l’impact socio-économique de la crise sécuritaire sur ses institutions de microfinance (IMF) partenaires, au cours de la période 2020-2025. Selon le directeur général de l’ANPFI, Wango Fidèle Yaméogo, cette étude vise à disposer « d’une lecture objective, documentée et partagée des effets de la crise sécuritaire sur les institutions de microfinance partenaires de l’ANPFI ». « Ce rapport provisoire couvre la période 2020-2025 et dresse un état des lieux sans complaisance, mais aussi des pistes pour renforcer la résilience du secteur », a-t-il indiqué. L’étude intervient dans un contexte marqué par une profonde évolution de l’environnement dans lequel opèrent les institutions de microfinance. Confrontées aux difficultés liées à la crise sécuritaire, celles-ci s’efforcent de maintenir leurs activités, de préserver leurs services et de continuer, autant que possible, à accompagner leurs clients et les populations bénéficiaires. Pour le directeur du suivi, de l’évaluation, des études et de la capitalisation de l’ANPFI, Kalidou Ky, l’étude vise à mieux cerner les difficultés rencontrées par les institutions de microfinance partenaires dans la mise en œuvre des conventions, notamment dans le déploiement des produits et services financiers, afin d’apporter des réponses adaptées. Il a également expliqué que cette étude intervient au moment où l’ANPFI travaille à l’élaboration de la deuxième génération de la stratégie nationale de la finance inclusive. Cette nouvelle stratégie devra notamment prévoir des mesures destinées à mieux accompagner les institutions de microfinance partenaires. Selon lui, l’étude a permis de recueillir et d’analyser des informations sur les évolutions enregistrées entre 2020 et 2025, tout en mettant en évidence les stratégies développées par les institutions concernées pour s’adapter au contexte sécuritaire. À travers cette étude, l’ANPFI entend ainsi disposer de données permettant de mieux prendre en compte les difficultés des institutions de microfinance partenaires dans les futures orientations en matière de finance inclusive. items.title: 6 countries that have qualified for every FIFA Women’s World Cup
items.description: Only six countries have maintained a perfect record of qualification for every edition of the FIFA Women’s World Cup since the tournament was first staged in 1991. The United States, Brazil, Germany, Norway, Sweden and Japan have all featured at every Women’s World Cup, making them the only nations to have achieved the feat. The Women’s World Cup has been held nine times, beginning in China in 1991, with the 2027 edition set to take place in Brazil. Here are the six countries that have never missed the tournament. 1. United States The United States is one of the two teams to have appeared at every Women’s World Cup. The Americans have also been the most successful nation in the competition’s history, winning the title four times. Their triumphs came in 1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019. The US have consistently been among the leading contenders at the tournament and have never failed to qualify since the competition began. 2. Brazil Brazil is the only South American nation to have participated in every edition of the Women’s World Cup. The Brazilian women have enjoyed a long-standing presence on the global stage, with their best performance coming in 2007 when they finished runners-up. Brazil have also produced some of the most celebrated players in women’s football, including the legendary Marta, and have remained regular contenders for the title. 3. Germany Germany has also qualified for every Women’s World Cup since the inaugural tournament in 1991. The European powerhouse has won the competition twice, lifting the trophy in 2003 and 2007. Germany’s consistency has made it one of the most successful teams in Women’s World Cup history, with the country regularly reaching the latter stages of the tournament. 4. Norway Norway is another European country that has never missed a Women’s World Cup. The Scandinavian nation won its only title in 1995 after defeating Germany in the final. Norway has remained a regular presence at the tournament and has also reached the final on two occasions, underlining its status as one of the competition’s historic teams. 5. Sweden Sweden has maintained a perfect qualification record since the first Women’s World Cup in 1991. Although the country is yet to win the tournament, Sweden has repeatedly gone deep into the competition. The Swedes have finished runners-up once and have also claimed multiple third-place finishes, making them one of the most consistent teams in the tournament’s history. 6. Japan Japan completes the exclusive list of six countries to have appeared at every Women’s World Cup. The Asian nation reached the pinnacle of women’s football in 2011, defeating the United States on penalties in the final to win its first world title. Japan subsequently finished runners-up in 2015 and has remained one of Asia’s strongest representatives at the global tournament. The six nations therefore stand alone in Women’s World Cup history for their remarkable consistency, having never missed an edition since the competition was launched in 1991. items.title: ‘We truly care’ – UGMC responds to allegations of poor-quality care
items.description: The University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) has reaffirmed its commitment to quality patient care amid criticism of its services, urging patients and their relatives to use the hospital’s established complaint channels when they have concerns. The response follows criticism of the facility after Ghanaian-American comedian Michael Blackson publicly raised concerns about the care his mother received at the hospital before her death. Speaking on JoyNews’ News Desk on Monday, August 10, Head of Public Relations and Client Services at UGMC, Barbara Hemeng, said the hospital takes concerns about patient care seriously and uses feedback to improve its services. Read Also: Michael Blackson blasts UG Medical Centre over mother’s death “At UGMC, we truly care about our patients, and we take reviews very seriously,” she said. Ms Hemeng also expressed sympathy to families who have lost loved ones at the facility, acknowledging the pain and distress associated with such experiences. She explained that the hospital continuously monitors feedback from patients and their relatives to identify gaps and improve service delivery. Read Also: UGMC demands retraction, apology from Michael Blackson over ‘worst hospital’ claim However, Ms Hemeng urged patients and families not to resort to social media as their first option when dissatisfied with the care they receive, arguing that formal complaints provide the hospital with an opportunity to investigate specific concerns and take appropriate action. “Going on social media to vent out your spleen does not help us improve upon our services. Let us all remember that UGMC is for all of us,” she said. She encouraged patients and relatives with concerns about treatment or service delivery to lodge complaints through the hospital’s established channels to enable the relevant departments to investigate and respond appropriately. UGMC maintains that patient feedback remains an important part of its efforts to improve the quality of care and services at the facility.

items.title: El incendio de Niebla (Huelva) está “fuera de la capacidad de extinción” y obliga a desalojar a 800 personas tras afectar a más de 20.000 hectáreas
items.description: El incendio declarado el pasado jueves en Niebla (Huelva) ha obligado este lunes a realizar un nuevo desalojo preventivo de unas 300 personas residentes en la localidad sevillana de El Madroño y la zona de Las Delgadas, en el municipio onubense de Zalamea la Real. Estas se suman a las casi 500 que permanecen desplazadas de Berrocal y aldeas como El Pozuelo o Marigenta desde última hora del sábado. La decisión ha sido tomada por la dirección de la emergencia ante la posible evolución de las llamas hacia las poblaciones y que pueda afectar también a las rutas de salida. El fuego sigue esta jornada en una situación de “extrema complejidad” y “fuera de la capacidad de extinción”, según ha advertido Antonio Sanz, consejero de Presidencia, Sanidad y Emergencias de la Junta de Andalucía, quien ha explicado que el fuego ha afectado ya a más de 20.000 hectáreas. También ha explicado que no ha habido “ninguna ventana de oportunidad para atajarlo” y que la lucha está siendo “ una carrera de fondo y con obstáculos cada vez más difíciles ”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: UGMC demands retraction, apology from Michael Blackson over ‘worst hospital’ claim
items.description: The University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) has demanded a retraction and apology from Ghanaian American comedian Michael Blackson over his description of the facility as the “worst hospital in Ghana.” UGMC says the comments have damaged its reputation and do not reflect the hospital’s clinical standards or overall performance. Read Also: Michael Blackson blasts UG Medical Centre over mother’s death Speaking on JoyNews Desk on August 10, the Director of Medical Affairs Dr Baffour Gyan said the assessment of a hospital should be based on its performance records, infrastructure and qualified personnel not an individual’s experience. “To come out and say UGMC is the worst hospital that one I disagree totally,” he said. Dr Gyan said UGMC is pursuing Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation as part of efforts to meet international standards and position the facility for medical tourism. UGMC management also rejected allegations of misdiagnosis or negligence in the treatment of Blackson’s 83-year-old mother. According to Dr Gyan, she was referred to UGMC from another facility with a severe infection and spent eight weeks at the hospital, including six weeks in the Intensive Care Unit. He said clinicians followed standard treatment protocols throughout her admission. “For diagnosis and management, 100% we did not do anything wrong,” Dr Gyan said. He added that the infection with which she was admitted was ultimately responsible for her death. Dr Gyan, however, expressed condolences to the family, acknowledging the difficulty of losing a loved one despite efforts to save them. UGMC has confirmed that its lawyers have formally written to Blackson over his social media comments. Dr Gyan said the hospital is seeking a retraction and apology and is awaiting the comedian’s response. “Our lawyers have written to him just for him to retract and apologise for all that he said on social media,” he said.

items.title: X1 Division One League Super Cup launched as Attram De Visser draw 3-3 with Debibi United
items.description: Attram De Visser staged a spirited second-half comeback to draw 3-3 with newly promoted Premier League side Debibi United as the fifth edition of the X1 Division One League Super Cup got underway at the Len Clay Stadium in Obuasi on Monday. The Accra-based side found themselves 3-1 down in the opening Group A fixture after Debibi United took control of the game, but goals from Abdul Majid Maswud and Thomas Okyere completed the comeback and earned Attram De Visser a point. Debibi United opened the scoring through Ibrahim Alhassan before Attram De Visser Junior restored parity to make it 1-1. Kwadwo Antwi then restored Debibi United’s lead before Clement Nketiah extended their advantage to 3-1. Attram De Visser responded through Abdul Majid Maswud to reduce the deficit before Thomas Okyere completed the comeback with the equaliser. The result saw both teams pick up a point as Group A action began, with former Premier League campaigners Real Tamale United scheduled to face Cape Coast Mysterious Ebusua Dwarfs in the second match of the opening day. Before kick-off, Obuasi Municipal Chief Executive, Hon. Faustilove Appiah Kannin, performed the ceremonial kick-off to officially launch the fifth edition of the competition. Attram De Visser’s comeback was inspired by Abdul Majid Maswud, who was named Man of the Match after scoring his side’s second goal. “We were giving up, but our coach backed us up with his words and motivated us to come back and equalise when we were down,” Maswud said after the game. “The group is very tight and the teams are well experienced and good. So, we have to come up with a good game and good tactics so that we can overcome them and, at the end, become the winners.” Debibi United assistant coach Francis Makiya attributed the collapse to a lapse in concentration after his side had built a two-goal lead. “We led 3-1, but I think in the last hour, there was a lack of concentration from my boys and Attram were able to come back,” Makiya said. “I think they’re doing well, but there is more room for improvement.” For Attram De Visser coach Godwin Attram, the tournament provides an important opportunity to assess his squad ahead of the new season. “It’s a very exciting pre-season tournament and good for the players,” Attram said. “We just want to see team organisation, structures, advantages and disadvantages of how the team attack and defend.” The tournament is sponsored by Hoshii International Limited, producers of X1 Energy Drink and Hoshii Instant Rice, with the company represented at the opening day by Ivy Udanoh. Udanoh said the partnership is aimed at strengthening the company’s connection with football supporters while creating greater brand awareness. “Ultimately, the partnership will help us build brand awareness and also get a stronger connection with the football community,” Udanoh said. “So far, it’s been positive and quite exciting to see people passionate about football coming together to support their team and the brand as a whole.” The opening Group A fixture produced a six-goal thriller, setting the tone for the remainder of the competition as the participating clubs continue their preparations for the new campaign.

items.title: World’s oceans hit record-high July temperatures
items.description: The world’s oceans hit their hottest-ever recorded temperatures in July, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions in the Pacific , according to the EU’s climate monitoring service. The average sea surface temperature (SST) outside the world’s polar regions – between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south – was 20.96C last month, beating the previous high of 20.89C, set in 2023. Last month was the joint second-warmest July globally on record, with temperatures 1.47C above the estimated pre-industrial average, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service. Meanwhile, Western Europe experienced its hottest ever June and July, with prolonged hot and dry conditions fuelling extreme wildfires across the region. Elsewhere, the UK is braced for its fifth heatwave of the year this week , as persistent dry weather puts further pressure on water supplies and could see more areas officially declared in drought. Around Europe, sea surface temperatures in July reached record highs along the Atlantic coast and in the western Mediterranean, contributing to widespread strong and severe marine heatwaves. Sea temperatures remained exceptionally high across much of the tropical Pacific, where El Niño conditions are developing and forecast to strengthen in the coming months. El Niño is a natural weather pattern in the Pacific that combined with human-driven global warming can cause temperature spikes and more extreme weather. Oceans are a vital regulator of the climate, absorbing most of the excess heat generated by greenhouse gas emissions and producing half of Earth’s oxygen. The greatest effect of ocean warming is on sea level rise. As seawater warms it expands, and this thermal expansion accounts for roughly a third of sea level rise recorded by scientists to date. That water encroaches on low-lying coasts and island nations. Hotter seas are also driving longer and fiercer marine heatwaves, which have bleached coral reefs on a mass scale and decimated kelp forests and fisheries. Warmer ocean surfaces also evaporate more heat and moisture into the air, intensifying tropical storms and loading them with heavier rainfall. ‘Climate change is intensifying heat extremes’ Western Europe is experiencing an exceptional run of extreme heat – with record-breaking temperatures in June and July, and some areas facing their third or fourth heat wave since May. The average temperature across western Europe for June and July was 21.62C – 2.79C above average and the highest for the two-month period. “July 2026 was the third consecutive month of exceptional heat in western Europe,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over the region, she said, while dry soils reduced the ability to provide natural cooling. “This is a clear example of how climate change is intensifying heat extremes, with heat and drought increasingly reinforcing one another,” she added. France, Spain, parts of Germany and the UK recorded exceptionally low rainfall and/or soil moisture, while soil moisture levels across much of western Europe were significantly lower than in 2022, when the region experienced severe drought. River levels have been much lower than average – in some places exceptionally low -with the Seine, Rhine and Danube among those particularly affected. Low flows exacerbate pressure on water supplies and irrigation, aquatic ecosystems, river transport and energy production. Some rivers in Europe have recorded extremely low water levels, including the Danube The prolonged hot and dry conditions have created favourable conditions for wildfires, with massive wildfires raging across western Europe last month and “exceptional activity” in terms of the area burned and smoke and emissions generated. “Climate change is increasingly bringing the kinds of hot and dry conditions that favour large, high-intensity wildfires in southern Europe while extended the fire season northwards,” said Laurence Rouil, director of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service. Larger fires produce more smoke and inject it higher into the atmosphere, allowing it to travel much further, he said. That means countries that experience relatively few wildfires could be increasingly affected by smoke traveling long distances. Extreme weather ‘new normal’ European wildfires haven been called “completely unprecedented” this summer In the UK, meanwhile, the prolonged dry spell is increasing pressure on already-stretched water supplies. England and Wales recorded their driest July since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, while large parts of England and all of Wales have already been officially declared in drought. The Environment Agency has warned that more areas of England could be declared in drought if dry conditions persist. Weather that was once considered extreme is becoming the “new normal”, according to the latest Met Office report on the UK’s climate. Its latest assessment found that the hottest day of the year in southern England is now 4.5C warmer than it was between 1961 and 1990. “We are right now living in a time of historic and unprecedented change,” said Mike Kendon, Met Office climate information scientist, adding that “evidence shows the climate of the 20th century has now gone”. Scientists say El Niño may temporarily push global temperatures even higher. Its effects are being felt against a backdrop of man-made warming, particularly the burning of fossil fuels. The world is now about 1.4C warmer on average than it was in the late 19th Century.

items.title: Tonto Dikeh launches New Wine Prophetic Tabernacle in Abuja
items.description: By Adewale Adesewa Tonto Dikeh has launched a new faith-based initiative, the New Wine Prophetic Tabernacle (NWPT), which she describes as a spiritual gathering for committed Christians. The 41-year-old Nollywood actress made the announcement on Sunday through her Instagram page, explaining that the platform is intended to serve believers seeking a deeper relationship with God and a renewed spiritual experience. According to her, NWPT is envisioned as a movement that will inspire spiritual awakening among Christians, encouraging them to live with greater devotion, purity, and purpose. She noted that the initiative aims to promote prayer, revival, and transformation across different denominations. Dikeh emphasised that the tabernacle is not structured as a church, but rather as a meeting point for individuals who are dedicated to spiritual growth and committed living. She described it as a space where believers can experience God’s presence and pursue a more intentional faith journey. The ministry will host weekly fellowship meetings every Friday at 6:00 p.m. at Omini Grand Hotel, formerly known as Alexis Hotel, located upstairs by Masalachi Junction in Jabi, Abuja. Her move into ministry follows her public declaration of faith, marking a significant shift in her personal life. Dikeh has previously shared her personal experiences of transformation, stating that she overcame several challenges after embracing her faith. In recent months, she has also taken part in spiritual activities, including conducting a deliverance session for a secondary school student. items.title: GoldBod to roll out gold traceability system this year – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says Ghana is set to begin implementing a national gold traceability system this year to track gold purchased from small-scale miners. According to him, the absence of a formal traceability system has meant that GoldBod currently cannot determine what proportion of the gold it purchased from small-scale miners was responsibly mined. Mr Gyamfi made the disclosure in response to questions about GoldBod’s purchase of 3.1 million ounces of gold from small-scale miners, compared with 2.8 million ounces produced by the large-scale mining sector. Asked what percentage of the 3.1 million ounces could be traced to responsibly mined gold, he told ‘Beyond The Numbers’ Isaac Kofi Agyei that there was currently no component that could be traced. “There is no component that we can trace because since Ghana started mining gold and trading gold, no government has pursued a traceability system,” he said on JoyNews. He, however, noted that GoldBod has developed a responsible sourcing policy which prioritises traceability and is now taking steps to implement a system capable of tracking gold from its point of origin. “We are currently involved in a national competitive tendering process to acquire that traceability technology. Following which, the onboarding process of eligible licensed small-scale miners or registered cooperatives will begin,” he explained. Mr Gyamfi said 27 companies submitted bids for the traceability system, with the process now narrowed to about 17 companies following the completion of the technical evaluation. “We’re going onto the financial proposal to evaluate that, and then we’ll be awarded. I don’t think that the process will go beyond this year for the system, and we will get a system done in the next few months,” he said. He stressed, however, that acquiring the technology would only constitute the first stage of the process. According to him, the system is expected to eventually enable GoldBod to trace every gram of gold it purchases and sells back to its mine of origin. The system will also help establish whether the source is licensed, how the gold was produced, whether mercury was used and whether child labour was involved. Mr Gyamfi said the broader objective is to formalise gold production and bring Ghana’s small-scale mining supply chain into compliance with international responsible-sourcing standards. He believes this will strengthen Ghana’s ability to access premium international markets, including the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), and secure better prices for the country’s gold. “How can we formalize those sources to be OECD compliant so that we can get LBMA market access for our gold and get better prices, better value, which means more revenue from our gold resources?” he asked. He added that the onboarding of eligible small-scale miners onto the system is expected to begin this year. “So that is what we are developing, and I can tell you that the system we acquired this year and implementation in terms of onboarding will start this year,” Mr Gyamfia added.

items.title: IGP promotes 25 police personnel over robbery, cocaine interception operations
items.description: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Christian Tetteh Yohuno has promoted 25 police personnel for their roles in a series of operations that led to the arrest of robbery suspects and the interception of suspected cocaine at the Tema Harbour. According to a post shared on Facebook by the Service on Monday, August 10, the personnel, drawn from the Bono East, Tema and Western Central Police Regions, were recognised for their involvement in three separate operations, including the arrest of six suspects in connection with a robbery involving GH¢300,000, the apprehension of four suspected members of a robbery syndicate and the seizure of 866 parcels of suspected cocaine. The promotions, according to the IGP, were based on performance and contribution of the personnel to the investigations and operations. One of the operations for which the personnel were recognised was a robbery on July 19 along the Portor to Kawempe stretch off the Kintampo-Buipe Highway. Six suspects were arrested in connection with the robbery, during which GH¢300,000 was reportedly stolen from a victim. The operation formed part of the police response to robbery-related incidents along the highway and resulted in the arrest of the suspects believed to have been involved in the incident. The personnel involved in the operation were subsequently considered for promotion based on their contribution to the arrests. Another group of personnel was recognised for their role in the arrest of four suspected members of a robbery syndicate linked to a violent robbery at Wassa Akropong in the Tarkwa area. The third operation involved the interception of 866 parcels of suspected cocaine at the Tema Harbour. It said the seizure represents one of the major drug interceptions cited by the police administration. Personnel involved in the operation were recognised alongside officers who participated in the robbery investigations in Bono East and the Western Central Police Region. The circumstances surrounding the shipment, including its intended destination and the identities of persons linked to it, were not detailed in the announcement. Among those promoted are Chief Inspectors Bede Nwinbomeh and Joe Tetteh, who have also been granted automatic entry to the Police Academy. Other promoted personnel include General Sergeants Elijah Ndaga Yinimi and Kaifan Sulemanna, as well as General Corporals Owusu Ansah Evans and Tansang Jonathan. General Lance Corporals Osei Christopher Bonny, Kyei Francis, Ofori Francis, Anim Dominic and Asante Isaac were also promoted. General Constables Adam Bakari Alhassan and Bakai Mark are among those elevated to their next ranks. The detective personnel promoted are Detective Chief Inspector Frank Dzah; Detective Inspectors Edem Ametowoga, Abroso and Vincent Dankwah; and Detective Sergeants Salifu Yakubu and Samuel Mordzifa. The police administration said six other personnel were also promoted to their next ranks in recognition of their contribution to the fight against crime. Chief Inspectors Nwinbomeh and Tetteh’s automatic entry to the Police Academy represents an additional recognition of their service. The IGP and members of the Police Management Board (POMAB) congratulated the promoted personnel and urged them to maintain the standards that led to their elevation. The police administration also indicated that it would continue to recognise personnel whose work contributes to crime prevention, investigations and public safety.

items.title: Yaadga : l’AJUD-BF invite la jeunesse à se placer au cœur du développement
items.description: Yaadga : l'AJUD-BF invite la jeunesse à se placer au cœur du développement Ouahigouya, 10 août 2026 ( AIB)- Dans sa dynamique d'éveil de conscience de la jeunesse, l'Association des jeunes unis pour le développement du Burkina Faso (AJUD-BF) a organisé le samedi 8 août à Ouahigouya, un panel afin de susciter l'engagement des jeunes pour le développement à travers la RPP, a constaté l'AIB sur place. Ce panel qui a rassemblé un parterre de jeunes et anciens, a été placé sous le thème, « Participation citoyenne à la sécurité nationale et contribution des jeunes à la Révolution progressiste populaire ». Dans le message du Gouverneur de la région de Yaadga, livré par son conseiller technique Issouf Savadogo, il a indiqué que le développement socio-économique du Burkina Faso est une affaire de tous. C'est pourquoi il a salué les membres de l'AJUD-BF pour leur initiative. « Le progrès prend sa source dans la prise de conscience surtout chez les jeunes. L'activité de L'AJUD-BF vient à point nommé et nous espérons que la population de la région s'impliquera pour soutenir les autorités de notre pays », a précisé le représentant de l'autorité suprême régionale. Le commandant de la deuxième région militaire, le camarade Lieutenant-colonel Lassané Porgo, venu soutenir l'initiative, a exhorté les participants au panel, à majorité jeunes, à faire corps avec les FDS et VDP pour restaurer l'intégrité territoriale. Pour lui, la Révolution progressiste populaire prônée par le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré donne une place privilégiée à la jeunesse et la met au cœur du changement. » Il est donc nécessaire que chaque citoyen s'investisse, joue sa partition pour un Burkina Faso nouveau débarrasser de la domination extérieure », a-t-il soutenu. Le Vice-président chargé des questions de développement de la commission nationale de l'AES, Adama Siguiré, a livré une communication sur la thématique du panel. A l'en croire, les jeunes doivent cultiver l'honnêteté, la vertu et le patriotisme vrai aux côtés de nos FDS et VDP pour venir à bout de l'hydre terroriste. » La RPP est une opportunité pour que la jeunesse dessine le « Burkindlim » authentique en vue d'imprimer les racines du développement endogène », a-t-il dit. Le président du comité d'organisation Abdoul Kader Touré par ailleurs Président de l'association, a indiqué que ce panel vise à terme, un changement qualitatif des jeunes par rapport non seulement à la sécurisation du pays qui incombe à tous les Burkinabè, mais aussi à leur appréhension du devenir du pays des hommes intègres. L'engouement suscité au cours des débats montre à souhait que la frange jeune épouse les idéaux de la RPP qui trace les sillons d'un développement harmonieux du Burkina Faso basé sur la collaboration civilo-militaire », a-t-il mentionné. Le Président Touré a saisi l'opportunité du panel pour remettre des attestations de reconnaissance à des personnalités engagées à leur côté. Avant le panel, les membres de l'AJUD-BF, autorités administratives et coutumières ont procédé à un reboisement dans l'enceinte du bloc des écoles « Bimbili »de Ouahigouya afin de reverdir l'espace de récréation. Agence d'Information du Burkina KNI/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: Health groups reject Tobacco Control Act amendment bill
items.description: …Warn proposed law could allow online sales of vapes, nicotine products By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Nigeria Tobacco Control Community, a coalition of more than 100 civil society organisations and health advocates, has rejected the National Tobacco Control Act (Amendment) Bill 2025, warning that the proposed legislation could weaken existing safeguards against tobacco and nicotine products. The coalition, at a press briefing in Abuja on Monday, urged the National Assembly to recall the bill for a comprehensive and transparent public health review. Executive Director, Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA), Akinbode Oluwafemi, described the proposed amendments as a “sham”, arguing that they could create loopholes for tobacco and nicotine companies to expand their activities in Nigeria. The bill seeks to amend the National Tobacco Control Act 2015 and its 2019 Regulations. While acknowledging the need to update the existing law, the coalition faulted several provisions of the proposed amendment, particularly those relating to non-combustible tobacco and nicotine products, including vapes, heated tobacco products and nicotine pouches. The coalition said Clause 1(n), which introduces “tobacco harm reduction objectives”, could be used to promote newer nicotine products under the guise of reducing harm. It argued that products marketed as less harmful were not necessarily safe, particularly for young people. The groups also faulted Clause 16, which excludes non-combustible products from the definition of tobacco products. “Heated tobacco products contain real tobacco. Heating it instead of burning it does not remove its toxicity,” the coalition said, adding that such products should be regulated as tobacco products. The coalition further expressed concern over Clause 7, which would permit advertising of non-combustible products in “adult publications”, at points of sale, online and through event sponsorship. It said the bill’s definition of an adult publication as one with at least 50 per cent adult readership could expose children to tobacco advertising. The groups also opposed Clause 9, which they said would remove the ban on internet and mail-order sales of non-combustible products where age verification measures were in place. According to the coalition, such measures could be bypassed, allowing adults to purchase products on behalf of minors. The proposed changes to health warnings also came under criticism, with the coalition alleging that Clause 12 would reduce warnings for vapes to text covering not more than 30 per cent of the packaging, while nicotine pouches would carry warnings covering 10 per cent. It further claimed that e-cigarette devices would be exempted from the requirement. The coalition also faulted Clause 10 for deleting specific penalties for selling tobacco products to minors and violating packaging requirements. It expressed concern over the Third Schedule, which it said would allow manufacturers to produce their own safety data while requiring the Minister of Health to keep the information confidential. The groups also opposed Paragraph 21, which they said gives the Minister of Health powers to exempt products “in the public interest” without clearly defined criteria. The coalition alleged that the provisions were not contained in the original HB 47 and HB 1151 presented at a public hearing on November 22, 2024. “Who introduced these provisions? Which public-health institutions reviewed them? The public has been completely excluded,” it asked. The groups acknowledged some provisions they considered positive, including the extension of smoke-free zones to 30 metres around schools and hospitals, as well as the proposed inclusion of the Police and Ministry of Youth in the Tobacco Control Committee. However, they said the provisions could not justify what they described as the more problematic amendments. The coalition demanded that the National Assembly recall the bill for a public health-led review and publish all relevant reports and submissions. It also called on the Federal Ministry of Health to clarify its position on the bill and demand its recall if it was not adequately consulted. The coalition further urged President Bola Tinubu to withhold assent if the bill is transmitted to him in its current form. Also speaking, the in-country coordinator, Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids, Michael Olaniyan, said the concept of harm reduction should not be used to weaken tobacco control measures. “Harm reduction is not harm elimination. What we want is to eliminate, not reduce,” Olaniyan said. The coalition called for a single, product-neutral tobacco control law covering all tobacco and nicotine products, insisting that advertising, sponsorship, sampling and online sales should remain prohibited. It urged Nigerians, particularly parents, health workers, young people and the media, to speak out against what it described as attempts to weaken public health protections. items.title: Why I shaved my hair for my wedding – Jarvis
items.description: By Caleb Ayemere Digital creator Amadou Elizabeth Aminata, popularly known as Jarvis, has addressed public speculation surrounding her decision to shave her head ahead of her recent wedding ceremonies, clarifying that the choice was purely practical rather than rooted in traditional marriage rites. Addressing rumors that the haircut was part of a tribal marital ritual, Jarvis took to social media to dispel the narrative, explaining that the decision was based strictly on professional hairstyling advice. According to Jarvis, her hairstylist recommended shaving her head to ensure a seamless fit for her hair extensions and wig installations, citing her natural hair texture as a challenge for achieving the desired bridal look. “I shaved my hair because I wanted my hair installation to be perfect,” she stated, noting that her natural hairline had previously made it difficult to secure frontal wigs neatly. “That is what my hairstylist recommended because I have stubborn hair.” The creator urged followers and observers to refrain from spreading unverified claims regarding cultural customs, reaffirming that the adjustment was strictly a beauty and styling preference for her wedding celebrations. items.title: Séguénéga : le district sanitaire mobilisé contre les moustiques lors des journées anti-vectorielles
items.description: Séguénéga : le district sanitaire mobilisé contre les moustiques lors des journées anti-vectorielles Séguénéga, 10 août 2026 (AIB)–Le district sanitaire de Séguénéga a organisé du 8 au 9 août 2026 les Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV), où à l'occasion, les populations ont été invitées à faire de la destruction des gîtes larvaires, un réflexe quotidien, a constaté l’AIB. Les dites journées qui visent à réduire la transmission du paludisme à la source, ont été placées sous le thème, «Ne soyons plus complices des moustiques, détruisons les gîtes larvaires». Selon le Plan stratégique national de lutte contre le paludisme 2021-2025, l’objectif est de réduire l’incidence du paludisme d’au moins 75% par rapport à 2015, soit de 380 à 95 cas pour 1000 habitants. Pour atteindre cet objectif, plusieurs interventions sont mises en œuvre dans les domaines de la prise en charge, de la prévention, de la surveillance et de la communication. Au cours de ces JNLAV, plusieurs activités ont été menées dans le district. En effet, une sortie de plaidoyer avec les leaders communautaires et administratifs, en passant par la mobilisation sociale, la cartographie des gîtes et des zones prioritaires et la destruction des gîtes ont été faites en collaboration avec les ménages. Les équipes ont ciblé les eaux stagnantes, les pneus usés et les déchets favorables à la prolifération des moustiques. Pour les deux journées de campagne, au total 3874 concessions ont été visitées et 2956 gîtes ont été identifiés. 97,87% de ces gîtes ont été détruits. « Nous avons également cartographié 58 gîtes larvaires difficiles à éliminer. Un suivi particulier sera fait sur ces sites », a indiqué le Médecin chef du district (MCD) Dr Fabrice Zongo. Les autorités sanitaires invitent les populations à adopter la destruction des gîtes larvaires comme un réflexe quotidien afin de protéger les ménages contre le paludisme. En rappel le district sanitaire de Séguénéga couvre les communes de Séguénéga, Kalsaka, Rambo et Kossouka. Agence d’Information du Burkina LG/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: EOCO escalates Ghana investigation into Asante Berko bribery case after US conviction
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has escalated its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the bribery case involving former Goldman Sachs investment banker and former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director, Asante Kwaku Berko. The development follows Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States in connection with allegations of bribery arising from his period in the private sector. In a statement issued on Monday, August 10, 2026, EOCO said it received a request last year from its counterparts in the United States in connection with investigations into the alleged bribery scheme. The request sought information on specific individuals in Ghana who were considered relevant to the investigations, including a former Minister of State and public servants. “Following receipt of the request, EOCO, in collaboration with the Attorney-General and Ministry of Justice, commenced preliminary work in relation to the Ghanaian aspects of the matter,” the Office said. EOCO said it also closely monitored the proceedings in the United States because of the international dimensions of the case. “Given the nature of the allegations and the international dimensions of the case, EOCO considered the evidence emerging from the U.S. proceedings to be potentially material to determining the appropriate scope and direction of any comprehensive investigation in Ghana,” it said. The Office explained that its approach was deliberate, stressing that investigations must be properly grounded in evidence and capable of supporting subsequent criminal proceedings and asset recovery where appropriate. “EOCO’s responsibility is not merely to commence investigations for the sake of public perception, but to ensure that investigations are properly grounded in evidence, conducted lawfully and capable where appropriate of supporting subsequent criminal proceedings and asset-recovery action,” it said. Following the conclusion of the US proceedings and Mr Berko’s conviction, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice engaged the appropriate US authorities to obtain relevant evidence, records and information required to advance the Ghanaian investigation. EOCO said the Attorney-General has subsequently directed it to escalate its investigations as the relevant information and official records are obtained from the competent authorities in the United States. “EOCO has accordingly commenced the process of intensifying its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the matter,” the Office said. EOCO stressed that the investigation will be conducted independently and in accordance with Ghanaian law. It cautioned that Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States does not automatically establish criminal liability against any individual in Ghana. “Any individual whose name appears in evidence obtained through the international cooperation process will be assessed independently on the basis of the evidence relevant to that person and in accordance with Ghanaian law,” it said. The Office said its collaboration with US law enforcement authorities and the Attorney-General’s Office remains active. It added that it would not disclose sensitive operational information that could compromise ongoing investigations, the integrity of evidence or any future prosecution. EOCO assured the public that further information would be provided at the appropriate time.

items.title: L’Algérie fait don de 4 hélicoptères et d’équipements militaires à l’armée nigérienne
items.description: NIGER-ALGERIE-DON-HELICOPTERES L’Algérie fait don de 4 hélicoptères et d’équipements militaires à l’armée nigérienne Ouagadougou, 10 août 2026 (AIB) – L’Algérie a remis, dimanche 9 août 2026, un ensemble de matériels composé de quatre hélicoptères et d’équipements militaires à l’armée nigérienne, dans le cadre du renforcement de la coopération bilatérale entre les deux pays, sur instructions du Président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a annoncé le ministère algérien de la Défense nationale (MDN) dans un communiqué. Le Chef d’état-major de l’Armée nationale populaire (ANP), le Général d’Armée Saïd Chanegriha, ministre délégué auprès du ministre de la Défense nationale, a ordonné la remise de ce don à l’armée nigérienne, en exécution des instructions du Président Abdelmadjid Tebboune, selon le communiqué. Le don est composé de deux hélicoptères de type MI-24V et de deux autres de type MI-171, qui ont décollé dimanche de la Base de déploiement secondaire d’In Guezzam, dans la 6e Région militaire algérienne, à destination de l’aéroport de Niamey, précise la source. Le lot comprend également des munitions pour les quatre hélicoptères, des pièces de rechange ainsi que du matériel d’appui, de maintenance et de soutien logistique, acheminés à bord d’un avion militaire des Forces aériennes algériennes. Selon le MDN, cette opération vise à consolider les relations fraternelles et historiques entre l’Algérie et le Niger et traduit l’engagement d’Alger à poursuivre son soutien aux pays de la région dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, de l’échange d’expertise et du soutien multiforme. L’Algérie entend également poursuivre ses efforts, en coordination avec ses partenaires, pour contribuer à la sécurité et à la stabilité dans la région. Agence d’information du Burkina

items.title: OPHK troops foil ISWAP attack on Borno base, recover weapons
items.description: …Several terrorists neutralised, soldiers injured By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have foiled an attempted attack by Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists on a Forward Operating Base (FOB) in Gajiram, Nganzai Local Government Area of Borno State. The Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday in Maiduguri. Goni said the attack occurred at about 12:20am on Monday when a large number of terrorists attempted to overrun the troops’ position. He said the troops responded with sustained fire, forcing the attackers to withdraw after suffering heavy casualties. “During the engagement, troops neutralised several of the terrorists and recovered weapons, ammunition and communication gadgets,” he said. According to him, surveillance footage reviewed after the engagement also confirmed several casualties being evacuated by the fleeing terrorists. He said the recovered items and surveillance footage were undergoing further operational assessment. Goni, however, disclosed that some troops sustained injuries during the engagement after part of the defensive position was temporarily breached. He said some combat equipment and vehicles were also damaged by Rocket-Propelled Grenade (RPG) fire. The injured personnel were promptly evacuated by air and were receiving medical attention in stable condition, he added. Following the attack, Goni said troops remained deployed in and around the FOB and adjoining areas to dominate the general area, monitor developments and prevent further attempts by the terrorists to re-engage. He urged residents of Gajiram and neighbouring communities to remain calm and continue their lawful activities, while encouraging members of the public to report suspicious movements or activities to security agencies. He said troops remained on high alert in and around Gajiram as exploitation of the operational area and further assessment of the terrorists’ casualties and activities continued. Goni said the Theatre Command, Operation HADIN KAI, remained committed to sustaining pressure on ISWAP terrorists until lasting peace and stability were restored in the North-East. The post OPHK troops foil ISWAP attack on Borno base, recover weapons appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigéria : l’État de Kano finance un mariage collectif permettant l’union de 1 500 couples
items.description: L'etat de Kano, dans le nord du Nigeria, a ete le theâtre d'un mariage collectif, le 7 août, unissant 1 500 couples lors d'une ceremonie organisee par le gouvernement local. Des celebrations ont egalement ete organisees dans les 44 zones administratives de la region, dans le cadre d'une initiative des autorites visant a aider les familles modestes ou a faibles revenus a couvrir les frais des mariages. Cette initiative s'adresse aussi aux veuves, aux personnes divorcees, aux femmes et aux hommes celibataires, ainsi qu'a toute personne ayant des difficultes a financer les frais de mariage. Les autorites ont mobilise des fonds de plus de 1,5 milliard de nairas (environ 1,1 million de dollars) pour ce programme baptise Auren Gata. Selon le gouverneur de l'etat, Abba Kabir Yusuf, chaque mariee a recu une dot de 200 000 nairas (environ 145 dollars), ainsi qu'un capital pour lancer une petite entreprise. Tous les couples ont d'ailleurs eu droit au mobilier (un lit, un matelas, une armoire, des couvertures, des draps et un tapis) et a des produits de premiere necessite pour leurs nouveaux menages. Remplir les conditions juridiques, religieuses et sanitaires pour se marier Cite par des sources de presse africaine, le Conseil de la Hisbah de l'etat de Kano, organisateur de cette initiative, a fait savoir que plus de 5 000 candidatures avaient ete deposees, mais que seulement 3 000 avaient ete retenues. La selection des futurs epoux s'est faite au terme d'examens medicaux comprenant des tests de depistage du VIH, de l'hepatite et des verifications de compatibilite genetique. Des verifications qui devaient assurer, selon les responsables du programme, la conformite des couples aux conditions juridiques, religieuses et sanitaires avant la ceremonie. La ceremonie s'est tenue dans la mosquee centrale de Kano, ou les unions etaient celebrees selon le rite islamique, ce qui n'empeche pas les couples chretiens de participer a l'initiative, comme ce fut le cas en 2023, lors d'une edition precedente du meme programme. Promouvoir la stabilite sociale dans l'etat de Kano Abba Kabir Yusuf a qualifie l'initiative d'« intervention sociale audacieuse visant a redonner espoir et a soutenir une vie familiale digne a Kano ». Outre le fait d'aider les femmes a se marier, le programme vise a « renforcer les familles et a promouvoir la stabilite sociale dans l'etat ». Pour le gouverneur, le mariage collectif s'inscrit dans les efforts plus larges des autorites locales en matiere de protection sociale et de renforcement de l'institution familiale, ainsi que de paix et de cohesion sociale. Il a par ailleurs appele les nouveaux maries a bâtir leurs nouveaux foyers sur la base de la patience, de la justice et du respect mutuel.

items.title: Attempt to associate GoldBod with losses is far-fetched — Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has rejected attempts to associate the state gold-buying agency with losses, describing such claims as “far-fetched”. Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod operated as a buying agent for the Bank of Ghana in 2025 and was entitled to fees for its services, similar to the arrangement that existed under the Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC). Speaking on JoyNews’ Beyond the Numbers on Monday, August 10, he explained that GoldBod initially received the same fees that had been paid to PMMC but subsequently reduced the charges as the volume of gold purchases increased. “I’m explaining to you that for 2025, the Gold Board continued as a buying agent, just like the PMMC. And we’re entitled to fees that the PMMC was paid. Same fees,” Mr Gyamfi said. He said GoldBod reduced the fees from 0.75 per cent to 0.6 per cent in October 2025, before cutting them further to 0.35 per cent in January 2026. “In fact, it was the Gold Board that reduced the fees from 0.75% to 0.6% in October 2025. And there’s evidence. Because the scale of the gold purchase has gone up,” he said. According to the GoldBod CEO, the agency eventually ended its role under the programme in February 2026 and no longer depended on the Bank of Ghana for fees. “And by the end of February, we ended the programme. And so now we do not depend on the Bank of Ghana for any fees because we now control the trade from the beginning to the end. And we fend for ourselves. That is what it is,” he explained. Mr Gyamfi’s comments come amid discussions over losses associated with the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP) and whether fees paid to GoldBod contributed to those losses. He disputed the suggestion that GoldBod’s fees could be used to explain the losses attributed to the central bank. Referring to an IMF assessment cited in a recent report on the Bank of Ghana, Mr Gyamfi said the figures showed a significant difference between the alleged losses and the fees paid to GoldBod. “The IMF claims that the losses the Bank of Ghana recorded under DGPP, which I cannot validate. But let’s assume they are correct. They say it is 17% of the value of gold bought by the Bank of Ghana,” he said. Mr Gyamfi questioned how fees of less than one per cent could reasonably be used to attribute the much larger losses to GoldBod. “So how does fees amounting to 0.758%, assuming without admitting that that is even a cost, what is the percentage of 0.758% of 17%?” he asked. He therefore dismissed what he described as an attempt to blame GoldBod for losses recorded by another institution. “So this whole attempt to tag the Gold Board with losses is far-fetched,” Mr Gyamfi said. The GoldBod CEO also used the interview to present the organisation’s 2025 financial performance, arguing that its own audited accounts do not support claims that the institution made a loss. He referred to GoldBod’s annual report and financial statements and invited viewers to examine the figures contained in the report. “This is the annual report. I’m giving you a free copy,” he told the programme. Mr Gyamfi directed attention to page 16 of the report, which contains the statement of financial performance for the year ended 31 December 2025. He said that the financial statements were published by the Auditor-General and were therefore not figures prepared by him or GoldBod management. “And if you go to page 16, this report was published by the Auditor General of Ghana, not Sammy Gyamfi, the Auditor General of Ghana,” he said. According to the figures he presented, GoldBod recorded total revenue of GH¢5.5 billion in 2025, compared with GH¢308 million recorded by PMMC in 2024. “Our total revenue, like you rightly said, was 5.5 billion from 308 million in 2024,” Mr Gyamfi said. Mr Gyamfi also pointed to what he described as a reduction in expenditure despite GoldBod operating with a much larger workforce than PMMC. He said PMMC recorded expenditure of GH¢129.6 million in 2024, while GoldBod’s expenditure for 2025 stood at GH¢109.5 million. “Despite revenue being tripled by the Gold Board, our expenditure rather was reduced,” he said. “In 2024, expenditure of PMMC was 129.6 million. But expenditure for Gold Board in 2025 was reduced to 109.5 million.” He said the reduction was achieved even though GoldBod had more than 450 workers, compared with fewer than 120 workers at PMMC. Mr Gyamfi argued that the figures demonstrated what he described as prudent financial management by the new institution. “And this was despite the fact that the PMMC had less than 120 workers, but the Gold Board had over 450 workers,” he said. “Despite having over 450 workers, more than double the workforce of PMMC, we displayed frugality, modesty, and prudence in expenditure and reduced expenditure from 129.6 million in 2024 to 109.5 million.” Mr Gyamfi said the combination of increased revenue and lower expenditure resulted in a surplus of GH¢5.4 billion for GoldBod in 2025. “At the end of it, we recorded a surplus of 5.4 billion,” he said. He said the financial statements should be used to distinguish GoldBod’s own financial position from losses reported by other institutions. “So if anybody tells you that the Gold Board has made a loss, this is the audited financials of Gold Board published by the Auditor General of Ghana,” he said. Mr Gyamfi further rejected any suggestion that GoldBod should be counted among institutions responsible for losses recorded elsewhere. “And if somebody says that the Gold Board is part of loss declared by another institution, tell them that that is a lie,” he said.

items.title: Iran says Pak-Saudi-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US
items.description: Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday that the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “a sign of a change in the perception” of regional countries towards the United States. The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. “This development is a sign of a change in the perception of the countries of the region,” ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said while responding to a query during a weekly press briefing on Monday. “Considering the developments of the last two to three years, the countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false security brokers,” Iran’s state media quoted him as saying, referring to the United States. Baqaei further said that there was “no reason to worry that this treaty will be against Iran”, highlighting Iran’s deep religious, historical and civilisational ties with Pakistan, Turkiye and even Saudi Arabia. “This development is an important sign that the countries of the region have concluded that they cannot rely on and trust the claim of security provided by the United States and some other actors outside the region, and they are attempting to try another method; by relying on their own capabilities and perspectives,” IRNA quoted Baqaei as saying. “Any plan that is based on the geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly identifies the enemy and the threat, has a chance of helping to strengthen security and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy and its allies,” he added, referring to Israel. In response to a question about Iran’s willingness to possibly join the joint pact, Baqaei said Iran has always “emphasised pursuing security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries” and “free from the influence and destructive intervention” of foreign actors. “Those plans still exist and can certainly be updated in light of developments,” the spokesperson added. “We are in close contact with neighbouring countries and regional countries, and we hope that all countries will learn from the developments of the last two or three years and adopt the best path to strengthen the region’s collective security,” he said, according to IRNA . Asked about Pakistan’s invitations to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to visit Pakistan, Baqaei said, “This visit will take place whenever the time is right. Bilateral relations are mainly considered.” He added: “The relationship between Iran and Pakistan is a very important one. In the last seven or eight months, it has become even more important than before, for various reasons.” Pact aimed at regional peace, Dar tells Iran FM Later in the day, Deputy Prime Minister and FM Ishaq Dar “shared the contours” of the pact with Iran’s Araghchi in a phone call, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Dar underscored its “objectives of strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace and security”. FM Araghchi thanked his Pakistani counterpart for “sharing the key aspects of the agreement”, FO said. The two leaders also “exchanged views on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the region and efforts to promote peace and stability”. On Sunday, DPM Dar said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact. Dar said the pact was the “culmination of years of discussions and coordination”, adding that it was “purely defensive” in nature. “It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.” The deputy PM clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations. Dar speaks with Kuwait FM, others on pact Separately, Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah felicitated Dar on the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the FO said. The two dignitaries spoke late on Sunday and also “exchanged views on the regional situation, including occupied East Jerusalem”. They also discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and “matters of mutual interest, including the follow-up to FM Jarrah’s recent visit to Pakistan and further enhancing cooperation and investment in key sectors”. “The two sides agreed to remain closely engaged,” the FO added. The deputy premier also shared the contours of the pact with Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi and former Guinea-Bissau president General Umaro Sissoco Embaló. In a joint call with them late last night, Dar shared the agreement’s “significance for strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace, stability and security”, FO said. Dar and Tshisekedi also exchanged views on Pakistan-DRC relations and agreed on the importance of further strengthening bilateral cooperation, including through high-level exchanges. DPM Dar had also spoken to Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand a day ago. “The two exchanged views on the regional situation, including the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye,” the FO said. It added that Dar shared the “essence of the agreement” and the “joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

items.title: Ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday cancels live event after plagiarism row
items.description: Jason Arday has cancelled an appearance in London next month, following his resignation as a Cambridge professor in the wake of allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. Arday’s talk at the Royal Geographical Society’s conference has been “cancelled at the request of the speaker”, the organisation said. He is also no longer listed on the websites of two other events scheduled for the coming months. Arday – who became Cambridge’s youngest ever black professor in 2023 – has admitted errors in his early work, but said he was not a “liar” and that the recent furore had led to “an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack”. He had been due to take part in a “fireside chat” at the Royal Geographical Society’s conference in London on 2 September. Arday’s appearance at Topping & Company book shop in Edinburgh on 18 September is no longer listed on the website and has reportedly also been cancelled. The shop declined to comment. He was also announced as a guest for the Arizona Women’s Board Authors’ Luncheon on 24 October, but is no longer listed on the event’s website. He is still listed as a speaker for the Stroud Book Festival in Gloucestershire in November. ‘Relentless accusations’ The publisher of Arday’s memoir Great and Unfortunate Things is going ahead with its release in the US on Tuesday and in the UK on 27 August as planned. The book tells the story of his life from being non-verbal until the age of 11 and unable to read or write until 18, then going through a series of “improbable triumphs and heartbreaking setbacks”, before being appointed professor of sociology of education at Cambridge. However, he has been accused of plagiarism in his PhD thesis, and questions have been raised about the reliability of parts of his life story, including that he ran 600 miles in six days and that he had raised £5.5m for charity. On Wednesday, the University of Cambridge said it had launched an investigation “following new information” about his “academic qualifications and honorary appointments”. Announcing his resignation on the same day, Arday said the “personal cost” of the scrutiny had become “too great”. He said: “While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement. “The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love.” He stressed that his resignation should not “be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me”.

items.title: WhatsApp : l’Algérie met en demeure Meta sur les comptes anonymes
items.description: L’Algérie a adressé une mise en demeure au géant Meta sur les comptes anonymes de la messagerie WhatsApp, a indiqué le ministère de la Poste et des télécommunications ce lundi 10 août. Ce dernier indique suivre de près l'activation de la fonctionnalité « Noms d'utilisateur » (usernames) sur WhatsApp en Algérie. « Cette fonctionnalité permet aux utilisateurs de s'inscrire et de communiquer sans divulguer leur numéro de téléphone », explique le ministère en annonçant avoir saisi officiellement par courrier Meta. Que demande l’Algérie ? Comptes anonymes de WhatsApp : ce que réclame l’Algérie de Meta Le ministère précise qu’il « n'a aucune objection à l'utilisation de cette fonctionnalité, notamment du point de vue de la sécurité et de l'expérience utilisateur, qui ne dépend pas du partage de son numéro de téléphone ». Toutefois, il réclame que « tout compte WhatsApp actif ou activé en Algérie doit être lié à un numéro de téléphone mobile valide qui a été enregistré auprès d'un opérateur mobile algérien. » Le ministère demande aussi au géant américain des réseaux sociaux (Facebook, Instagram) de « fournir une réponse écrite confirmant que chaque compte WhatsApp utilisé en Algérie reste lié à un numéro de téléphone valide et vérifié », et qu'il « n'autorisera pas la création ni la gestion de comptes reposant uniquement sur un nom d'utilisateur, sans lien avec un numéro de téléphone ». Le ministère de la Poste et des Télécommunications demande aussi à la multinationale fondée par le propriétaire de Facebook, Mark Zuckerberg, un « plan de mise en œuvre précis, assorti d'un calendrier, pour toute adaptation technique spécifique au marché algérien ». Cette demande est « nécessaire et proportionnée, et qu'elle ne porte pas atteinte à la vie privée des utilisateurs ni au chiffrement de bout en bout », précise le ministère. Pour lui, l'objectif est de garantir la « confiance et la responsabilité numériques », et de contribuer à la « prévention de la fraude, de l'usurpation d'identité et de la cybercriminalité, conformément à la législation algérienne en vigueur ». L’article WhatsApp : l’Algérie met en demeure Meta sur les comptes anonymes est apparu en premier sur TSA .
